name: 熊魚菴 たん熊北店 東京ドームホテル店 (Yugyoan Tankuma Kitamise — Tokyo Dome Hotel)

claims.text: Dishes are prepared in a kitchen shared across the restaurant's full menu, using shared cooking and washing equipment, so trace amounts of allergens (including wheat) may be present even in dishes without wheat as a listed ingredient.

Guests with food allergies or disliked ingredients (seafood, meat, dairy, buckwheat, wheat, etc.) are asked to contact the restaurant directly by phone rather than note it in the online reservation comment field, so staff can discuss options before the visit.
The restaurant states its dishes are not a complete allergy-accommodation menu and that it may decline to serve guests with severe allergy symptoms, for the guest's own safety.
The restaurant proactively publishes an allergy-handling policy and invites direct phone consultation before the visit, rather than ignoring the topic.

Standard soba tsuyu uses regular shoyu, which contains wheat; wheat-free tamari not confirmed available

name: アトミヨソワカ 蔵前店

claims.text: Entire facility is wheat-free — no wheat flour handled anywhere, which removes the main celiac risk.
No published formal cross-contamination protocol or GF certification; a strict celiac should confirm shared-equipment handling.
Uses JAS oatmeal — confirm oats are certified gluten-free-purity if you are oat-sensitive.
Some items co-produced with an external welfare workshop (ろくえもん); its handling protocols not independently verified.
None — the whole facility is 100% plant-based, so no animal-product cross-contact.
Brand explicitly caters to wheat-allergy and egg-allergy diners and to vegans/food minorities ('小麦アレルギー・卵アレルギーの方、ヴィーガン、フードマイノリティの方').
No wheat, egg, dairy, or refined white sugar used anywhere.
Fully vegan and gluten-free menu — every item is safe to order.
Rice-flour based; transparent about ingredient sourcing (Tosa Reihoku rice, JAS oats/agave, homemade apple yeast, domestic okara).
No preservatives.
